mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated WORKPLACES mobility indicates commuting demand is still depressed. That suppresses spontaneous retail visits, so RETAIL_REC will remain lower over the next four weeks unless WORKPLACES rebounds materially.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days while WORKPLACES stays at or below its current four-week level.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility falls week-on-week after a multiweek rise, discretionary outdoor activity is rotating away from leisure trips and toward home-based time. That shift should reduce retail-and-recreation visits within the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops at least 5 points from the prior weekly mean after rising for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after a qualifying PARKS drop, or instead rises above its last-four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays above its current baseline while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, people are concentrating activity at home and avoiding shared-trip shopping. That combination predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +4 and TRANSIT below -25 simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite the residential-high/transit-low condition persisting for at least two weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its already depressed level signals tighter movement frictions or weaker service use, which should curtail nonessential shopping trips almost immediately and push RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 after being above -27 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after TRANSIT crosses below -30, or the retail series strengthens instead.

mechanism_narrative: A broad shift toward home time, captured by RESIDENTIAL rising alongside WORKPLACES falling, indicates substitution away from out-of-home discretionary activity. Over four weeks this should keep retail-and-recreation mobility below its recent average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES does not recover.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS over the previous two weeks is a seasonal signal of warmer-weather outing behavior that spills into adjacent shopping trips. If PARKS keeps rising, RETAIL_REC should turn higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases for two consecutive weeks and remains above +15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of the PARKS upswing or stays below its recent four-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM holds near or above its current level while WORKPLACES remains weak, shopping demand is being satisfied by necessity trips rather than broader discretionary retail. That mix should keep RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above -10 while WORKPLACES stays below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days despite persistent high grocery/pharmacy mobility and weak workplace mobility.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable restriction regime, an improvement in TRANSIT paired with rising WORKPLACES means commuting capacity is recovering. That should translate into more incidental retail traffic and a higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days despite simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
